The empirical framework additionally recommends communicating design trade-offs and limitations to the whole team. (high confidence) — https://www.thinknpc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Co-design-guidance-July-2019.pdf · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Participatory design and accessible co-design · also: https://sjdr.se/articles/10.16993/sjdr.952
- [statement] NN/g treats fidelity as separable dimensions of interactivity, visuals, and content or commands. A prototype can be detailed in one dimension and rough in another. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ux-prototype-hi-lo-fidelity/ · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity
- [statement] Task-based prototype evaluation can observe people performing typical product tasks and use their mistakes and comments to find usability problems. Figma also recommends using user flows to guide test scenarios and the important steps to evaluate. (medium confidence) — https://www.leilatakayama.org/downloads/Takayama.Prototypes_HFES2002_prepress.pdf · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity · also: https://www.figma.com/resource-library/user-flow/
- [statement] Do not assume prototype timings or appearance ratings predict the finished product. A mobile-phone experiment reported possible overestimation of task completion time with a computer prototype and inflated aesthetic judgments for reduced-fidelity prototypes; MeasuringU’s review also finds weaker accuracy for task times and aesthetic measures. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18691696/ · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity · also: https://measuringu.com/prototype-fidelity/
- [statement] NN/g distinguishes clickable prototypes, whose action responses are prepared before testing, from static prototypes, whose responses a person supplies during testing. Pilot the prototype: NN/g warns that operator errors can affect the study. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ux-prototype-hi-lo-fidelity/ · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity
- [statement] Treat a prototype as a candidate design hypothesis: observe people using it, compare approaches and revise or discard ideas before committing to a build. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ux-prototype-hi-lo-fidelity/ · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity · also: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/design/making-prototypes
- [statement] Choose prototype detail and medium to fit the research question and practical constraints. Sketches can explore basic ideas; more realistic code or interactive prototypes support tests of realistic interactions. A mandatory paper-to-polished sequence is not established by these sources. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/design/making-prototypes · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ux-prototype-hi-lo-fidelity/, https://www.leilatakayama.org/downloads/Takayama.Prototypes_HFES2002_prepress.pdf
- [statement] For inclusive interaction testing, the GOV.UK Prototype Kit guidance identifies code prototypes as a way to test on the user’s own device and with assistive technology such as a screen reader; it also supports branching based on user input. The medium must support the interaction being investigated. (medium confidence) — https://prototype-kit.service.gov.uk/prototyping/ · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity · also: https://www.leilatakayama.org/downloads/Takayama.Prototypes_HFES2002_prepress.pdf
- [statement] Walker, Takayama and Landay’s controlled web-prototype experiment found no significant difference in the number or severity of usability issues across fidelity or paper/computer conditions, but did find differences in issue types by fidelity. This supports using low fidelity for some formative testing without assuming identical findings. (low confidence) — https://www.leilatakayama.org/downloads/Takayama.Prototypes_HFES2002_prepress.pdf · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity
- [statement] Advice about fidelity and willingness to criticize is qualified: NN/G argues that unfinished-looking prototypes can encourage negative feedback, whereas MeasuringU reports a study finding participants just as likely to offer critiques on paper and high-fidelity computer prototypes. Do not treat increased criticism from low fidelity as universal. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ux-prototype-hi-lo-fidelity/ · keywords: UI/UX design: inclusive systems, Task flows, wireframes and prototype fidelity · also: https://measuringu.com/prototype-fidelity/
